title: Extending proper base change from $\Dctf$ to the localizing closure
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and let all schemes below be separated and of finite type over $k$, and all arrows be $k$-morphisms. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring as in [sk-def-localizing-closure], with the finite-subextension convention for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ in [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For a scheme $T$ use the ordinary unbounded category $D(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$, its bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$, and its localizing closure $\Loc(\Dctf(T,\Lambda))$ [sk-def-localizing-closure].

Consider a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
p'\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$
with $p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Write $u^*$ for the exact module-object inverse image [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], also applied termwise on derived categories, and $Ru_*$ for the total right derived module-object pushforward, with adjunction $u^*\dashv Ru_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\theta:p'^*g^*\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^*p^*$ be induced termwise by the two module pullback composition isomorphisms [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] and the equality $g\circ p'=p\circ g'$. Let $\eta'$ be the unit for $p'^*\dashv Rp'_*$ and $\varepsilon$ the counit for $p^*\dashv Rp_*$. Define the base change map by
$$
\beta_K:
 g^*Rp_*K\xrightarrow{\eta'_{g^*Rp_*K}}
 Rp'_*p'^*g^*Rp_*K\xrightarrow{Rp'_*(\theta_{Rp_*K})}
 Rp'_*g'^*p^*Rp_*K\xrightarrow{Rp'_*g'^*(\varepsilon_K)}Rp'_*g'^*K.
$$
If $\beta_K$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, then it is an isomorphism for every $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: Properness of p-prime follows from the chosen pullback square and properness under base change. Apply proper_image_localizing_proper_coefficients to both proper maps, separately for each of the six coefficient rings. Apply unboundedLocalizingPullback to g and g-prime. Their ambient sum-preservation clauses imply sum preservation for the two composites on diagrams of localizing source objects: for the second composite lift the pulled-back diagram into the localizing category of X-prime using the pullback localizing clause. This also treats the empty diagram.

proof.text: Use the coherent shift structure of the exact termwise inverse image, transported through leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory to the total left derived inverse image. The normalization isomorphism commutes with these shifts by the compatibility theorem for Functor.CommShift.ofIso. Exactness transfers through this isomorphism. Equip each right derived direct image with the shifts induced by its actual derived adjunction; the adjunction unit and counit commute with them and the right adjoints are triangulated. Their composites are triangulated. No new derived adjunction, exchange map, or coefficient object is chosen.

proof.text: Expand leftDerivedUpperStarComp into the exact-functor normalization, the localized termwise natural isomorphism and the localized composition isomorphism. The upstream Shift.ExactFunctor instances show that both localized isomorphisms commute with shifts. Cancellation of the normalization and its inverse proves shift compatibility of the composition comparison. The equality-induced comparison around the square also commutes with shifts, by substitution. Thus condensedAmbientPullbackComparison commutes with shifts. Expand mateEquiv: all units, counits, whiskerings, compositions, associators and unitors commute with shifts. The canonical ambient exchange consequently commutes with shifts; the generic triangulated-isomorphism-locus instance makes its isomorphism locus triangulated.

proof.text: Prove the localizing determination argument directly with L = localizingClosure S and P = L intersect eta.isoLocus. The localizing-closure existence theorem supplies that L is localizing. P is triangulated and replete by intersection. For a discrete diagram whose objects lie in P, lift it to L; Step 1 says that both functors preserve its ambient colimit. The whiskered natural transformation is an isomorphism since each component is, so isIso_app_coconePt_of_preservesColimit proves invertibility at the colimit. Together with closure of L this proves P localizing. If eta is invertible on S, every S-object belongs to P. The defining intersection formula for localizingClosure now puts every L-object in P. This is precisely determination on the localizing closure, without constructing restricted target functors.

proof.text: The termwise exchange is conjugate to the ambient exchange by the specified exact-functor normalization isomorphisms. Invertibility of their components gives equivalence of invertibility of the two exchanges on each object. Transfer the generator hypothesis to the ambient exchange, apply Step 4 with its triangulated isomorphism locus from Step 3 and sum preservation from Step 1, then transfer the conclusion back. Assemble the finite-ring, integral, rational, finite-intermediate integral and rational, and algebraic-closure cases by conjunction introduction. Use the bottom finite intermediate field when the proper-image coefficient list needs an otherwise irrelevant finite extension, and ZMod ell when it needs an otherwise irrelevant finite torsion ring.

statement_correction.reason: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the imported reference to the unit leaves the standing scheme hypotheses absent from its standalone statement and its statement dependencies. The proper-image coefficient assertions used by its proof require separated finite-type schemes over the standing positive-characteristic field. Properness alone does not imply those hypotheses: the identity on an infinite disjoint union of Spec(k) is proper but its source is not finite type over k. This is a failing applicability check, not a claimed counterexample to base change. Explicitly restore the source chapter standing setting, as already done in the reviewed proper-image prerequisite; spell out the same ordinary unbounded base-change morphism without altering its generator assumption or conclusion.
